definitions: A type of data relationship where one record (the master) controls the display and behavior of related records (the details).
A hierarchical link between two objects where the detail records are dependent on the master record for their existence and security.
examples: The invoice and its line items form a master-detail relationship.
In the database, we established a master-detail relationship between departments and employees.
Deleting the master record automatically deletes all associated detail records in a master-detail relationship.
